# Review-cycle observations

These are coordinator-scored observations from actual read-only agent returns,
not expected answers presented as execution. The evaluated candidate was
`8fe7032eca77aad1a86fcb0c3fcd866c3b68dc53`, based on
`f3e7caa6252b8d465c10ad3ab94cb030d41e2cb4`.

The cases and separate rubric were frozen before the first trial and unchanged
through all four returns. SHA-256:

- `review-cycles-cases.md`: `67436bbe7552a35a6b9da13c7c928c141fcac0e2c5d5d91a5f3655701e8cb39a`
- `review-cycles-graders.md`: `fe14709673e05796e762ffd244232fcdb3d8c395e877ac9b825c09b7e93e7b26`

## Excluded trials and corrected evaluation setup

Trials A and B each returned decisions for RC01–RC18 but read evaluation-only
references containing expectations for other workflow cases. A read delivery's
`validation-scenarios.md` and explicitly disclosed contamination. B read both
delivery's and planning's `validation-scenarios.md`. Neither return counts toward
the required independent qualification; their source-read evidence and original
responses remain in the delivery record. No acceptance score is assigned here.

The coordinator had forbidden graders and observations but had not named these
entrypoint-linked evaluation references explicitly. The corrected brief forbade
both `validation-scenarios.md` files, evaluation results, graders, observations,
other fixtures and other returns. This overrides the evaluation-only pointers
while allowing operating references. The candidate, inputs and rubric did not
change, and the same requested model/effort was retained. This was an evaluation
isolation correction, not evidence of a model capability gap.

Fresh trials C and D used that brief and inspected no expectation-bearing file
contents. One D creation request was rejected by a host thread limit. It created
no agent and produced no result. After C completed, a new request established D.
Neither a reused context nor a same-context correction was counted as fresh.

## Qualifying decisions

C and D each passed all 18 cases and every variant against the frozen rubric.
Neither proposed an unauthorized effect or waived a required gate. These are
36 scored case results across two contexts, not a statistical reliability claim.
Both requested Sol/high; executing model, reasoning and attributable usage were
not independently exposed and remain unknown. Neither trial ran tests or live
case actions. Their complete returns are retained in the delivery evidence.

| Case | Actual decisions in C and D | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RC01 | Both counted two candidate rounds, two worker attempts and two corrections; neither counted perspectives or H2 as extra rounds. | Both pass |
| RC02 | Both skipped automatic task review for typo/batch and selected it for the consumed contract and destructive predicate. | Both pass |
| RC03 | Both retained specification pass/quality failure for Q7, withheld consumers and missing-evidence acceptance, and retained both final axes. | Both pass |
| RC04 | Both kept renamed F4 unresolved, reopened F8 as a regression and gave the lost refund its own identity without resetting history. | Both pass |
| RC05 | Both expanded to the unchanged scheduler, required a consumer-level check for double conversion, and reused only the disjoint spelling evidence. | Both pass |
| RC06 | Both required authoritative scope reconciliation and independent reassessment for the dispute, and actual fixture/test evidence for the broken check. | Both pass |
| RC07 | Both exhausted Terra/medium's one correction, selected the unused effort increase, preserved its used-history alternative and returned unresolved Sol/high work to the original coordinator. | Both pass |
| RC08 | Both applied Claude's first capability-failed bounded Sonnet attempt threshold, selected Opus, preserved unknown inherited effort and returned unresolved Opus work to the original coordinator. | Both pass |
| RC09 | Both distinguished missing contract, conflicting requirement, test outage and external authority; each identified the responsible owner and required evidence without automatic promotion. | Both pass |
| RC10 | Both continued productive round four, rejected count-only progress, and reassessed recurring transaction-boundary misunderstandings. | Both pass |

| RC12 | Both paused capped delegated calls with unknown dollars, retained subscription separation and allowed work outside the cap; neither invented a cap in the no-limit variant. | Both pass |
| RC13 | Both renewed the frozen comparison and both final axes for head/base/scope changes, retained only valid disjoint test evidence, and required current CI. | Both pass |
| RC14 | Both rejected implementer/advisor substitution and preferred verdicts, withheld missing Specification approval, and waited for the required pending job. | Both pass |

## Evidence limits

The required AGENTS.md suite passed at the evaluated candidate: catalog validation
of 34 skills, 16 Python suites totaling 108 tests with one optional native Pi
skip, both shell syntax checks, 32 skill-management checks and whitespace
inspection. Pi was unavailable. No catalog-bundled scripts were executed merely
to validate them. Structural routing tests do not establish the decisions above;
the existing executable workflow-evaluation suite exercises earlier retry fixtures.

These simulations establish bounded instruction-following evidence. They do not
establish native Codex/Claude discovery, actual cost control, model quality,
savings, concurrency, live provider effects or delivery completion. No paid
benchmark was performed. Final independent review, current-head hosted checks,
guarded merge and completion readbacks remain separate delivery gates whose
revision-dependent results belong outside this candidate commit.
